desc: FROM IRC 2026-08-02: yuka told sven she has not seen the 'trying to write to read-only' SMP crash 'since a few weeks' but that 'it depends very much on the kernel config used'. That is (a) proof our 205 bug is a KNOWN M4 issue, not a Wallace bug, and (b) independent corroboration of our round-7 finding that rodata=full vs rodata=on changes the failure qualitatively (maxcpus=5: total hang -> full 5-CPU boot, no panic). ACTION: bisect the config. (1) Build with CONFIG_RODATA_FULL_DEFAULT_ENABLED=n rather than the rodata=on cmdline -- the two paths do not exercise identical code -- and retest maxcpus=5 with scripts/t6040-cow-repro.sh, >=4 runs, fresh baseline (208 method rule). (2) Diff our .config against a Fedora Asahi config and against yuka's branch defaults for MM/arm64 knobs: RODATA_FULL, DEBUG_PAGEALLOC, INIT_ON_ALLOC/FREE, PAGE_POISONING, KFENCE, SHUFFLE_PAGE_ALLOCATOR, VMAP_STACK, ARM64_16K_PAGES. (3) If a single knob fixes it, that is the answer AND a real contribution -- nobody upstream has isolated which knob matters. Our three-line reproducer is the tool they lack. ROUND 1 RESULT 2026-08-03: (a) rodata_full is a RUNTIME knob (pageattr.c), not a Kconfig symbol -- no CONFIG_RODATA_FULL_DEFAULT_ENABLED exists, so the cmdline was already the right mechanism. DEBUG_PAGEALLOC/KFENCE/PAGE_POISONING/SHUFFLE all off, so rodata=on genuinely disables the page-granular linear map. (b) rodata=on at maxcpus=5 is REPRODUCIBLE: boots 3/3 (654/637/557 lines, 5 CPUs, OpenRC, no panic, 3 traces each) vs 100% hang by default. maxcpus=14 still hangs. (c) ARM64_TLB_RANGE=n WITHOUT rodata=on gives the SAME profile at maxcpus=5 (635 lines, 5 CPUs, 3 traces, no panic) -- one boot only, needs repeating. (d) BOTH combined still hang at maxcpus=14. CONVERGENCE: two independent knobs that both REDUCE TLB-INVALIDATION WORK produce the same partial improvement, which fits every prior observation (faults on valid addresses, bulk ops as victim, severity scaling with CPU count since TLBI is broadcast, suppression by delays). But it is a SCALING effect not a fix: threshold moved ~3 -> ~5 cores only. NEXT SINGLE EXPERIMENT: CONFIG_ARM64_HW_AFDBM=n (hardware access/dirty-bit management) -- do_wp_page depends on dirty/AF bits and mishandled hardware DBM would corrupt exactly the CoW path. New kbuild switch T6040_NO_TLB_RANGE=1 (default off); baseline kernel rebuilt with TLB_RANGE=y restored. Daily driver stays maxcpus=1. ROUND 2 / CORRECTION 2026-08-03: HW_AFDBM=n gave the SAME profile at maxcpus=5 as rodata=on and TLB_RANGE=n (660 lines, 5 CPUs, 3 traces). Three unrelated knobs with identical results prompted the control I should have run first: the PLAIN BASELINE, freshly rebuilt, boots at maxcpus=5 too (556 lines, 5 CPUs, 1 trace). So ALL THREE KNOBS ARE IRRELEVANT and the "TLB-invalidation convergence" conclusion is WITHDRAWN. The real variable was the INITRAMFS: the "maxcpus=5 always hangs" evidence came from the 99 MB i3-image era, not the current 8.8 MB sdroot. Re-measured threshold, baseline config, one image throughout: 5 BOOTS, 6/7/8/10/14 all hang -- exactly the ORIGINAL maxcpus>=6 characterisation in ticket 121. The earlier "2 is the limit" was an artefact of the big image. STILL NOT USABLE: at maxcpus=5 with full init the system boots (702 lines) then throws 4 traces incl a FIFTH signature __pi_memset_generic <- ext4_mb_prefetch (bulk memSET) plus a killed process; neither shell nor SSH answered. maxcpus=1 remains the only clean config. METHOD FAILURE: experiments were compared against a baseline measured under a DIFFERENT payload -- the control must be re-measured in the same session/image/core-count.
